solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cavaliers not on form, it's said

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so the letters of the words before are rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: Royalist cavaliers are said to be out of form, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' looks like part of the surface ('not on form'), but it is fodder: CAVALIERS plus NOT ON make fourteen letters to rearrange, and 'form' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken in talk rather than written is described by this adjective, so a remark that is said aloud in chat qualifies.

clue.text: Having fun with Sooty, poor Corbett's initially ill-matched

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a sorry, broken state, so they are jumbled
initially says only the opening letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Children's TV puppeteer Harry Corbett, playing with his glove puppet Sooty, is clumsily out of step.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a long-running British children's TV glove-puppet bear, first worked by Harry Corbett. FUN and SOOTY are rearranged ('poor') and the C from Corbett is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things not synchronised in timing are mismatched, so the idiom means badly coordinated or not in harmony.

clue.text: Gesture at sea saving a cast

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
cast here means thrown out, so the letter a is discarded from the jumble

explanation.surface: A sailor on a ship makes a rude gesture while sparing a fishing cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SAVING and 'cast' throws out its A, leaving VSIGN. The V-sign, made with the palm turned inward, is a rude gesture in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-fingered hand signal is a rude British insult when the palm faces inward, so it is a kind of hand gesture.

clue.text: Worshippers of emperor raised on a remote island

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word for emperor is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tsar was the emperor of Russia
remote means far off

explanation.surface: Devotees of an emperor grew up on a far-flung island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TSAR upwards in this down clue to give RAST; 'on' simply stacks it above the rest. Neatly, the movement does venerate an emperor, Haile Selassie of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Jamaican religious movement that reveres Haile Selassie are collectively called by this name, so they are religious devotees.

clue.text: Cab heading off to the centre of Rome? That's taken for granted

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is cut away

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letters of the city's name

explanation.surface: Taking a cab into the middle of Rome is something you simply assume.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface is a question about a taxi ride, while the definition is the reply that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition accepted as self-evidently true without proof is a principle assumed from the start.

clue.text: One close to home is not joking

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
close to means near
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone living near home says they mean what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being serious and sincere, rather than kidding around, is the sense of this idiom.

clue.text: Computer company in flipping clouds

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: IBM is the famous computer company

explanation.surface: An irritated computer firm complains about blasted clouds, as in cloud computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses both pieces together, and also reads as a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin term for a grey rain-bearing cloud, these are dark rain clouds.

clue.text: Medicine for Norman you found in Boston area

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Boston, England, is in Lincolnshire, abbreviated LINCS
the Normans spoke French, and tu is French for you

explanation.surface: A cough remedy for someone called Norman turns up in the Boston area.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman looks like a man's name; it means the Normans' French. LINCS is Lincolnshire, an English county containing the town of Boston.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing syrup taken for coughs is a type of medicine.

clue.text: Room found by leader of Argonauts somewhere in Greece

parts.note: an attic is a room under the roof

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Jason, leader of the Argonauts, finds a room somewhere in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of Argonauts' tempts you toward Jason; it only means the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around Athens in Greece bears this name, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Africans with Egyptian king? Yes, in Italy!

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, was an Egyptian king
si is Italian for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Africans came with an Egyptian pharaoh and is told yes, in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: This people of Rwanda and Burundi are an ethnic group of central Africa.

clue.text: Superhero, doffing cap, reprimands vagrant

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders, so the letters wander out of order
doffing a cap means taking off what is on top, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A superhero politely tips his cap while scolding a homeless wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doffing cap' removes the R heading REPRIMANDS, and 'vagrant' rearranges the remaining EPRIMANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The web-slinging Marvel comic character is a famous costumed hero with powers.

clue.text: King's daughter at home with drink

parts.note: being in means being at home
Fanta is a brand of fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A royal princess relaxes at home with a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain and Portugal the title for a monarch's daughter is this word, a princess.

clue.text: Spoil team having gutted smart left-winger

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A smart team is ruined after losing a socialist player.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx's communist ideas is on the political left.

clue.text: Bottomless pit used by baby's mother

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bottomless pit is employed by a baby's mother, perhaps for dirty nappies.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic, poetic form of abyss, it names an immeasurably deep chasm.

clue.text: Declaration in Patent Office originally

parts.note: patent as an adjective means obvious, manifest

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A statement is lodged at the Patent Office in its first form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent Office' reads as one institution; split it, with patent as the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A public statement of a party's policies and aims is a formal declaration.

clue.text: A Democrat prepares info in mailing list

parts.note: to dress food, such as a salad or fowl, is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A US Democrat politician readies details for a campaign mailing list.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailing list holds the street details of where each person lives, so these are its entries.

clue.text: Give lines to old sculptor

parts.note: to donate is to give
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone hands lines of verse to an aged artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine Renaissance artist famed for his bronze David was a sculptor.

clue.text: Midriff revealed during important match

indicators.note: revealed during says one piece shows up inside another

parts.note: seminal means highly important or influential
read as mid-riff: the middle of the word riff, its two centre letters

explanation.surface: A footballer's bare stomach is exposed during a big cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'important match' reads as one definition, but 'important' is wordplay. Split 'Midriff' as mid-riff, the middle of the word riff; 'revealed during' places that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The round before the final of a knockout tournament is a decisive game between two sides.

clue.text: Dissonance died out, reuniting island

indicators.note: reuniting means joining the pieces together again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
out says that letter is removed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Discord fades as an island community comes back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'died out' removes D from DISSONANCE, and 'reuniting' rearranges the remaining ISSONANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This British territory in the South Atlantic is a remote volcanic island.

clue.text: State question that causes inflation

parts.note: to air a view is to state it
to pump someone is to question them for information

explanation.surface: A government asks which policy is behind rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The economic sense of inflation is the bait; the definition means blowing up tyres or balloons.
explanation.definitionFit: A device forcing gas into a tyre or balloon blows it up, so it brings about inflation literally.

clue.text: Herb's picked up daily

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: thyme is a herb; the possessive gives thyme's

explanation.surface: Someone's herb crop has been gathered from the garden every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The London newspaper of this name is a daily paper, published every day.

clue.text: Casual dress for old soldiers

definitions.meaning: tracksuits and sweatshirts are relaxed leisurewear
an old sweat is British slang for a veteran soldier

explanation.definitionFit: Tracksuit clothing goes by this plural, and British slang calls veteran troops 'old sweats', so both senses fit.

clue.text: Fluster-free?

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters before it are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A one-word description of a calm state with no flustering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' frees the letters of FLUSTER into a new order, and the whole clue also defines: without fluster is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calming and relaxing is free from agitation and bother.

clue.text: Paintings put up around grand Irish town

indicators.note: around says the reversed word encloses the letter
in a down clue put up means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: oils are oil paintings
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Pictures are hung around a grand building in an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: This county town in the north-west of Ireland is a town on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Lowest rent? About a shilling

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: to let a flat is to rent it out
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: A landlord asks the cheapest rent and is told roughly a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest rent' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Lowest'. The shilling was an old British coin worth one twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest in amount or degree is a superlative meaning lowest.

clue.text: Mycologist's last to put out fungus

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: to ruffle someone is to put them out, annoy them

explanation.surface: A fungus expert finally throws out a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The prized underground edible fungus is dug up by pigs or dogs, a delicacy mushroom.

clue.text: Part lukewarm revolutionary, part extremist

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
the second part says only a portion of the opening words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next; the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lukewarm radical, partly an extremist, describes a half-hearted firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden word no signal; the second 'part' supplies it, leaving 'extremist' as the definition. 'revolutionary' turns ARTLU, found across 'Part lukewarm', around.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardline partisan on the political fringe, especially a royalist or right-winger, is an extremist.

clue.text: Remove delay after loveless marriage

indicators.note: after places the following word behind the first piece
loveless means without love, the zero score O in tennis, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a marriage is a union
to stall is to delay

explanation.surface: Someone wants to stop putting off a split after a cold, loveless marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, hence O; 'loveless' drops it from UNION to give UNIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking software off a computer is to remove it, the computing opposite of installation.

clue.text: Belief not affected by reversal

indicators.note: not affected by reversal says the word reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A conviction that does not change when overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine held as true is a core belief.

clue.text: Expert helping friend with correspondence?

parts.note: a pro is an expert
a helping is a portion of food
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A specialist helps a friend deal with letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters; here it means matching in size or ratio, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in matching ratio means in correspondence, each part kept in relation to the others.
